Ben (support): Customer reported a 401 + latency spike on /v1/generate. They provided a 'request_id' string and an 'x-request-token' header value. Asking: can infra pull server logs for the request_id?
Ivy (eng): Which identifier do they mean — the client-side request_id or the internal request token? can you paste the exact values?
Ben (support): Copied from customer — request_id: r-8f3c2a1b and x-request-token: tk_7Yz9Q. They said it failed at 2026-03-16T18:23:12Z and got a 401 then 502.
Sam K (infra): Ok — two searches to try. Our log pipeline indexes both request.id and headers.x-request-token but under different fields depending on the service.
Sam K (infra): Kibana KQL (api service logs):
```
service.keyword: "api" and (request.id: "r-8f3c2a1b" or headers.x-request-token: "tk_7Yz9Q") and @timestamp:[2026-03-16T18:20:00.000Z TO 2026-03-16T18:30:00.000Z]
```
Sam K (infra): If you use the older logger index (raw-logs):
```
json.request.id: "r-8f3c2a1b" OR json.headers.x-request-token: "tk_7Yz9Q"
```
Raj (oncall): Note retention: default hot indices kept for 24 days. For infra-legacy we only have 14 days. If the event is older than retention we'll need the debug bundle from the customer or an on-host trace.
Ben (support): It's within 12 hours so should be fine. Running the KQL now.
support-bot: Debug bundle requested by Ben. Upload URL: https://internal/support/debug-bundles/2065432101 (expires in 48h) :inbox_tray:
Ivy (eng): If the KQL returns nothing, try searching by auth token fingerprint. Some services log a masked token like token_fingerprint: "tk_7Yz9Q". Query example:
```
service:auth and message:/tk_7Yz9Q/ and @timestamp:>= "2026-03-16T18:00:00Z"
```
Ben (support): KQL returned two hits in api-prod-2026-03-16: one shows 401 at the auth gateway, the other is the downstream 502 from model-proxy. Attaching snippet:
```
[auth-gateway] request.id=r-8f3c2a1b status=401 reason="invalid token" user_id=null
[model-proxy] upstream_request_id=up-44a2 status=502 downstream_err="connection reset"
```
Ivy (eng): Good. Next steps for repro bundle: ask customer to run curl with same headers + body and include x-request-id to match server logs. Example to send to customer:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <their-token>" -H "x-request-token: tk_7Yz9Q" -H "x-request-id: r-8f3c2a1b" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
Raj (oncall): Also request they enable debug (if safe) to capture client-side timings. If they can't reproduce, we have the server-side traces tied to request.id and upstream_request_id; we can correlate to the model-proxy trace id.
Ben (support): Sharing the two log lines and the reproduction curl with the customer now. Will ask them to upload the debug bundle to the support link.
Sam K (infra): For the ticket: include the two log hits, the KQL used, index names (api-prod-2026-03-16), and note retention policy (24d hot, 365d archived for enterprise). That lets SRE request archive retrieval if needed.
Ivy (eng): If the customer reports tokens rotated, remind them tokens are short-lived and can produce 401s after rotation — check the 'token_issued_at' vs event time.
Ben (support): Thanks team :thumbsup: I'll update the ticket when customer uploads bundle.
support-bot: Debug bundle uploaded by Ben: 2065432101-debugbundle.tar.gz (size 12MB) :file_folder:
